newsitem.title: USA: Comcel paying $38.9 mln for 10-year Colombia deal.
newsitem.headline: Comcel paying $38.9 mln for 10-year Colombia deal.

text.p: Communicacion Celular S.A. (Comcel) said Tuesday it will pay the Colombian government $38.9 million for a 10-year extension of its contract to provide cellular telephone service in the eastern region of Colombia.
Peter Burrowes, president of Comcel, said the extension lends greater certainty to the company's future and will allow it greater access to international capital markets to finance its expansion.

Comcel is one of six Colombian telephone companies whose contracts to provide cellular services in various regions was recently extended by the Colombian Ministry of Communications for 10 years. The six are to pay a total of $130 million for the contract extensions.
One of those companies, Occel S.A., said in a statement that it was awarded a contract extension to March 29, 2014 to provide cellular services in Colombia's western region.
Its initial contract expires on March 29, 2004, it said.
Mario Velez, an official of the company, said Occel will pay $16.6 million for the contract extension.
